conventions.convention: Probability measures on R carry the evaluation sigma-algebra; σ is the Gaussian standard deviation, and the mixture densities are positive, finite and jointly measurable.
Hellinger distance uses h²(p,q)=∫(√p−√q)², without a factor of one half. KL and log-square moments are taken under the truth, with logarithmic integrands zero where the truth density vanishes.
Dyadic scale bands are lower-closed and upper-open, retain the scale cutoff σ≤sₙ, and use location-tail tolerance min{rₙ,1/4}²/8.

The simplex neighborhood permits a zero-base residual cell, which then has zero random mass and is omitted; uniform constants for positive residual base mass require that mass to range in a fixed compact subset of (0,m].

The main theorem assumes AC, independent F and S, σ=σₙS, and both stated scale-tail bounds. Its conclusion is convergence in sampling probability at sufficiently large fixed multiples, without an almost-sure or generic minimax assertion.
Compact scale support removes the middle rate term. Removing the logarithm from the Gaussian-bias term additionally requires the corollary's finite-union support and interval-mass condition.

load_bearing.statement: On evaluation-measurable probability measures F on R, (F,σ,x)↦p(F,σ)(x) is jointly measurable, 0<p(F,σ)(x)≤1/(σ√(2π)) for σ>0, and ∫p(F,σ)(x)dx=1; it is the density of F*N(0,σ²).

There is a universal C such that, for A,σ>0, 0<η<1/2 and every probability F supported on [−A,A], a discrete probability F′ on [−A,A] exists with at most C max{A/σ,1}log(e/η) support points, L1 mixture error at most η and supremum mixture error at most η/σ.

Assume AC and a jointly measurable family of finite-valued densities against one sigma-finite measure for IID data. For 0<δₙ≤εₙ with nδₙ²,nεₙ²→∞, local KL and log-square prior mass at radius δₙ at least exp(−C₀nδₙ²), a measurable sieve with vanishing posterior complement, and a countable measurable partition with finite covering numbers Nₙⱼ on positive-prior-mass strata, the condition exp(−nεₙ²)Σⱼ√(Nₙⱼπₙⱼ)→0 implies posterior Hellinger contraction at every sufficiently large fixed multiple of εₙ in sampling probability.

Assume AC. For a nonnegative compactly supported C² probability density p with J=∫{p>0}(p″)²/p<∞, qσ=p*φσ satisfies ∫(p−qσ)²/qσ≤(4/9)σ⁴J, KL(p||qσ)≤(4/9)σ⁴J and ∫p[log(p/qσ)]²≤(4/9)σ⁴J, with logarithmic integrands zero where p=0.

Assume AC, a compactly supported C² probability density p₀ whose support K is a finite union of intervals, finite ∫{p₀>0}(p₀″)²/p₀, and P₀(I)≥cλ(I)^a for every interval I⊆K. For independent F~DP(α) and S~G, with α finite nonzero and having continuous strictly positive density near K, arbitrary probability G on (0,∞), polynomially bounded bandwidth n^(−a₁)≲σₙ≲n^(−a₂), 0<a₂<a₁<1, and σ=σₙS, both local KL quantities are at most C₁σₙ⁴ on a set of prior mass at least exp{−C₂σₙ^(−1)(log n)²}, eventually.

concerns.concern: Verification step 2.1 states: “σₙ² log n=n^(−2/5)(log n)^(4/5)” for σₙ=n^(−1/5)(log n)^(2/5). In fact σₙ² log n=n^(−2/5)(log n)^(9/5). Thus the two terms in its cited main-theorem rate do not balance, and that citation does not establish the asserted n^(−2/5)(log n)^(4/5) bound. That bandwidth and faster bound correspond to the interval-mass refinement, whose additional truth assumptions are absent from this example. The distinction also appears in [the source, Theorem 1, equations (2.1)–(2.2) and the following paragraph](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0708.1885).
